title: The AI Video Studio-in-a-Box
pitch: OpenMontage turns a plain-language brief into a fully produced video — script, generated clips, voiceover, music — but hands you a rendered file with no further control. OpenCut is a real, open-source editor shell waiting for an API and headless mode. Wire OpenMontage's production pipeline in as OpenCut's first 'AI assist' plugin: a client types 'make me a 30-second product teaser,' OpenMontage drafts the full rough cut, and it lands directly in an OpenCut timeline where the client can trim, re-voice a line, or swap a clip before export. That's a one-click first draft plus a real editor for the 10% a human always wants to touch — sellable to small agencies and solo creators as a monthly content-engine subscription instead of a per-video freelance invoice.
why_now: OpenMontage just showed agentic video production working end-to-end for pennies, and OpenCut's README explicitly says its rewrite is adding an Editor API and headless mode built for exactly this kind of integration — the plumbing for this mashup is being built on both sides this quarter.
